title: Why is a king holding the life sign?
surface: B92: south wall, west wing, middle register in situ (called third in the edition), third scene from the west.
researchQuestion: How does a small held object distinguish a deceased, deified king from an ordinary royal participant?

claims.text: The project caption identifies Sety I’s held ankh as an indicator of divine status in this scene.

citations.locator: Interior Wall Scenes: final caption Ramesses II purifies a statue of his deified father Sety I

claims.text: The commentary locates B92 on the south wall, west wing, in the middle surviving register, third scene from the west.
The scene began in raised relief and was converted to sunk relief; traces of earlier edges remain.
